h1: A web development company for New York firms that cannot afford a bad relaunch
intro: 22 Signals is a web development company New York firms hire for redesigns, migrations that keep search rankings, accessible builds, client portals and e-commerce. We plan the content and SEO before design starts, build on WordPress, Shopify or a custom stack, and look after security and updates once the site is live.

sections.h: What goes wrong with New York website projects
p: A redesign is often where a New York business loses ground it spent years earning. The new site looks better, launches on time, and then organic traffic falls sharply because old URLs were not redirected, location and practice pages were merged, or the developer blocked search engines on staging and forgot to undo it.

The second risk is legal. New York federal courts are among the busiest venues in the country for website accessibility lawsuits, and plaintiffs' firms test sites with screen readers and automated scanners. A site that fails basic checks, such as missing image descriptions, forms without labels or menus that cannot be used by keyboard, is an easy target.
When you choose a web development company, ask who is responsible for rankings and accessibility after launch, not only who designs the homepage.

sections.h: Accessibility and privacy built in, not bolted on
p: We build to WCAG 2.2 AA as standard. That means proper headings, alt text, color contrast, keyboard navigation, form labels and captions on video, checked with automated tools and by a person using a screen reader before launch. We avoid overlay widgets that promise instant compliance, because they do not fix the underlying code.

Forms are where a site collects private information. Under the SHIELD Act, a business holding personal data about New York residents needs reasonable safeguards, so contact, intake and payment forms go over encrypted connections, store only what you need, and send data to systems with access controls rather than a shared inbox. Cookie and tracking choices are set with your counsel.

sections.h: Proof: a client portal built for a US law firm
p: We built a client portal for a US law firm where clients log in to see their documents, sign what is needed and pay invoices, instead of chasing email attachments. The portal sits behind the same login and security rules as the rest of the firm's systems, and every document and payment leaves an audit trail. It is the kind of project where design, development, security and content all have to work together.

sections.h: How a build runs: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow
p: Talk: we look at your current site, analytics and search data before quoting. Plan: a sitemap, a redirect map for every ranking URL, content outlines and design direction, with dates agreed in writing. Build: design, development, accessibility testing and a staged launch with redirects checked. Grow: we monitor rankings and errors for the weeks after launch, fix anything that slips, and keep the site maintained if you want us to.

sections.h: Working with a web development company from London
p: We work with New York companies remotely from London. New York is five hours behind London for most of the year, so design reviews and stand-ups happen in your morning, and changes you request by the end of your day are often on the staging site when you start the next one. Launches are scheduled for low-traffic hours in Eastern Time, with our team watching.

Hiring a web development company New York staff have never met in person can sound risky. In practice the risk sits in the process, so ours is written down: who approves each stage, what counts as done, and the date. Website projects run well remotely: shared design files, a staging site you can click through and one Signal Lead who answers for the whole build. We visit New York when the project needs it.

faqs.q: Will a redesign hurt our Google rankings?
faqs.a: It should not, if it is planned properly. We crawl your current site, list every URL that earns traffic or links, and map each one to its new home with a permanent redirect. We keep titles, headings and content that rank, then monitor search data after launch and fix anything that slips quickly.

faqs.q: Do you build ADA-compliant websites for New York businesses?
faqs.a: We build to WCAG 2.2 AA, the standard courts and regulators most often point to, and test with automated tools and a screen reader before launch. No developer can promise you will never be sued, but a properly built accessible site removes the easy findings that most demand letters rely on.

faqs.q: Which platform do you recommend: WordPress, Shopify or custom?
faqs.a: WordPress suits content-heavy sites with many practice or service pages and lots of editors. A headless CMS with Next.js suits marketing sites that need strong design and simple editing. Shopify is our default for e-commerce. For portals and complex logic we build custom. We choose after seeing your content, team and integrations.

faqs.q: Do you meet clients in New York?
faqs.a: We work remotely from London with calls in your morning, and most website projects never need a meeting in person. If a kickoff workshop or a content session with your partners would help, we can come to New York when the project needs it.

faqs.q: Can you take over maintenance of our existing site?
faqs.a: Yes. We start with an audit of plugins, hosting, backups, security and accessibility, fix the urgent items, and then move to a monthly care plan with updates, monitoring and a set amount of change requests. If the site was hacked, we clean it first.

faqs.q: How much does a website from a web development company in New York cost?
faqs.a: It depends on templates, content, integrations, migration size and ongoing care. We do not publish prices, but after a 15-minute call we can give you a written estimate.
